topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding the complexity of complement nomenclature.

topics.label: Foundations of Complement and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overall architecture, historical naming conventions, and the pivotal biochemical activation of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement Activation Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that detect pathogens and converge to deposit C3b on target surfaces.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes triggered by complement activation to eliminate pathogens through opsonisation, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement activation and damage.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical presentations, susceptibility to infections, and autoimmune risks associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to subvert complement attack and how these bacterial factors are applied in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
